findings.body: A review containing only P2/P3 findings never produces a review_findings occurrence because this filter requires outcome failed or blocked. New evidence relevant to the ruling about exposing the latest open review result: src/forge/review.py:495–499 records outcome clean whenever no blocking finding exists, while retaining advisory findings. Prototype reviews similarly mark non-P0 findings clean. Those findings appear in the board's count but their review identity is omitted, so EVENTS cannot announce that the review found problems as detail 3 requires. Expose the latest result whenever it has undismissed findings, without changing merge gates, and extend the producer-backed command test beyond its P1-only case.
findings.title: Not done: expose the latest review's open advisory findings

findings.body: The JSON command tests cover runnable steps, waiting prose and human-only merge prose, but never assert null for a Forge command containing a placeholder or ensure that a later runnable Next line is not selected instead. This is an explicit detail 2 rule. For example, src/forge/nextstep.py:409–410 emits forge story done with an outcome placeholder after all tasks merge without a recorded outcome. Removing the placeholder rejection could advertise that command while the current assertions still pass. Add command-level coverage of this state, with a later runnable step present, asserting null in forge next --json and the story's board next.
findings.title: Not done: command test for a non-runnable first Next line containing a placeholder

findings.body: A failed result unconditionally overrides the item's saved status, even when the local branch has advanced beyond the PR head described by the response. The query requests headRefOid, but neither the board nor next-step callers compare it with the local head before passing fail here. After a local repair commit, an old-head failure can therefore keep advertising forge work instead of forge close; it can also replace a newer working stage. This differs from the ruled same-head rerun case: the failure belongs to another commit. Preserve the PR check display, but do not use that failure to override newer local work. The existing stale-head test uses successful checks only.
findings.title: Ignore previous-head failures when deriving the local next step

findings.body: The previous merge-detection gap remains: machine_board detects merged tasks and fixes only from state on the fetched default branch, both PR lookups request open PRs, and the story calculation receives an empty merged-PR set here. A PR merged on GitHub can consequently retain its old stage and merge/close advice until a fetch and subsequent board refresh. In contrast, src/forge/nextstep.py:189 obtains merged branches, and its _task implementation at lines 506–516 uses that evidence. Reuse it for machine task/fix stages and story next-step calculation.
findings.title: Recognize GitHub merges before the default branch is fetched

stop.done: src/forge/board.py is simpler and behaves as it did before
